attacker-influenced."},{"step":7,"file":"usbredirparser/usbredirparser.c","function":"usbredirparser_serialize","line":1705,"var":"write_buf_count_pos","code":"write_buf_count_pos = ~(USBREDIRPARSER_SERIALIZE_BUF_SIZE - 1);","note":"When the state grows beyond the default 64 KiB chunk, the serializer reallocates the backing buffer."},{"step":9,"file":"usbredirparser/usbredirparser.c","function":"usbredirparser_serialize","line":1712,"var":"wbuf","code":"if (serialize_data(parser, &state, &pos, &remain, wbuf->buf + wbuf->pos, wbuf->len - wbuf->pos, \"write-buf\"))","note":"A large number of buffered writes can force the serialization buffer to move while the saved patch pointer still refers to the old allocation."},{"step":10,"file":"usbredirparser/usbredirparser.c","function":"usbredirparser_serialize","line":1720,"var":"write_buf_count_pos","code":"memcpy(write_buf_count_pos, &write_buf_count, sizeof(int32_t));","note":"Root cause: the stale patch pointer may now point outside the reallocated buffer, so writing the count becomes an invalid write/use-after-free style memory-safety sink."}]
